images.date: Hull : Weston Tuxford Howe, Printer, [...]6, Scalb-Lane, 1843.

images.title: Transparent window shades

William Earle Smith, Philadelphia Transparent Oil Cloth Window Shade Manufactory, No. 92 Walnut St." Big wood-type headline, ornamental type border, small body text; a star-shaped cut-out of another copy sits on black board at right.

images.title: J. Hall Rohrman, ornamental japanner and manufacturer of grocers' tea chests, canisters and all kinds of japanned-ware, No. 96 Cherry Street, above Sixth, Philadelphia / E. Ketterlinus & Co., printers, Philadelphia.
images.archive_detail: Library of Congress
images.what_it_shows: Trade card / shop label, 1850: "J. Hall Rohrman, Ornamental Japanner and Manufacturer of Grocers' Tea Chests, Canisters and all kinds of Japanned-Ware, No. 96 Cherry Street, Philadelphia" (E. Ketterlinus & Co., printers). images.title: Cuckoo, from the Birds of America series (N4) for Allen & Ginter Cigarettes Brands
images.archive_detail: The Metropolitan Museum of Art

images.people_or_logos: none (small maker's line of defunct 1880s tobacco firm; the name was revived by Topps as a card-product name, note)
images.use: 03: Cut out; laid end to end along the strokes, inside the silhouette (treatment A). 25 distinct cards; the Manhattan Watch Co. card was removed (drawn figures).
images.research_notes: Best of the set: bird + roses, warm palette, crisp litho dots, flat scan on grey; cuts out as a clean rectangle. Same series, same scan style (Met Burdick, Allen & Ginter Birds of America N4, 1888, all PD with images, all bird+flower, no people): 406620 Cuckoo, 406621 Osprey, 406622 Goldfinch, 406629 Crossbill, 406632 Woodpecker, 406634 Dipper, 406635 Wren, 406636 Albatross, 406638 Catbird, 406641 Kingfisher, 406644 Martin, 406647 Raven, 406650 Mockingbird, 406656 Starling, 406657 Chickadee (~50 in series). Large-format versions: N37 (4216xx-4221xx) and Birds of the Tropics N38 (4207xx-4213xx), but those carry cigarette packs/brand panels. Alternate people-free set at the Met: Old Judge 'Flowers' series (Goodwin & Co., 1890; 400534-400599, e.g. 400543 Poppy, 400581 Sunflower, 400568 Pansy) - single flowers, only the flower name printed, no brand on the face. Rejected sets: Kinney 'Novelties' N228 die-cuts (all show women's faces), A&G 'Fruits' N12 (children). | Credit: The Jefferson R. Burdick Collection, Gift of Jefferson R. Burdick. Medium: Commercial color lithograph. Artist: Allen & Ginter.

images.title: La Belle Jardinère: le magasin de la rue de la Cité pendant sa demolition, Paris
images.archive_detail: Cleveland Museum of Art
images.what_it_shows: Charles Marville albumen print, Paris 1864-66: the side wall of the La Belle Jardinière store painted with giant letters 'MAISON DE LA BELLE JARDINIÈRE' and two painted prize-medal roundels, standing over a demolition site
images.people_or_logos: Left painted medal shows a large profile portrait of Napoleon III ('Medaille d'honneur ... 1855') - a drawn face: crop it out. No photographed people (wheelbarrows, carts, demolition rubble only). La Belle Jardiniere is a defunct Paris clothing-store brand.
images.research_notes: Very strong era material: one of the earliest photographs of a hand-painted wall advertisement (1864-66), frontal, even daylight, huge condensed slab-serif letters 'BELLE JARDINIERE' (~2400 px wide in the full file) plus 'MAISON / DE LA', right-hand painted medal with coat of arms. Use the lettering band / right half as texture B or C; avoid the left medal. Sepia albumen tone, fine grain. CMA record id 439499. Technique: albumen print from collodion negative. Credit: Gift of Michael Mattis and Judith Hochberg.

images.title: Lands and Homes

images.research_notes: Best wood-type broadside in the Smithsonian CC0 set: big, inky display type, real paper tone. Photographed inside a clear sleeve, so a little glare at the margins; crop to the printed area. Also works as C (dense type with the mark cut out). Undated in the record (railroad land sales of the 1870s-80s).

images.title: Salon Shop Sign
images.archive_detail: Smithsonian Open Access - National Museum of American History (nmah)
images.what_it_shows: Lithographed/enamelled tin sign by American Art Works (Coshocton, Ohio), 1920s-1970s: orange ground, black border, "AUTHORIZED AGENT Mme. C. J. Walker's SYSTEM AND PREPARATIONS". Rolled edge, scratches and star-shaped punched nail holes.
images.people_or_logos: none. BRAND FLAG: the Madam C. J. Walker name is the whole subject. The original company closed in 1981, but the name was relaunched as a beauty line in 2016 (Sundial Brands/Unilever), so treat it as a possible living brand.
images.research_notes: Technically the best pressed-tin image in the Smithsonian: a genuine tin advertising sign from one of the big tin-sign makers, 11014x8260, white background, real wear. Usable as B by cropping the orange enamel field with the punched holes; using the whole sign depends on the director's call on the brand. Provenance: Marjorie Joyner's Chicago salon, an important African American history object, so handle it respectfully. Smithsonian alternates (not downloaded): NMAAHC "Sign for authorized agent of Mme. C.J. Walker's" NMAAHC-2013_153_6_001 (12592x11813, same brand), NMAAHC Pullman "Pullman passengers only" sign NMAAHC-2014_63_63_18_001 (3970x6649), NMAH Woman Suffrage Bluebird tin sign NMAH-ET2015-20047 (1915, die-cut), NMAH Baltimore Equitable Society fire mark NMAH-AHB2006q06209 (cast iron, about 1400 px object).

images.title: SHAC advertising stamp case

images.research_notes: True pressed-metal advertising with crisp raised lettering and soft highlights, 2000x2000. The object is tiny (3.3 cm), so the scan is its full detail. Aluminium, not tin, but it reads as pressed tin.

images.title: "General Delivery" sign

images.people_or_logos: none (U.S. Post Office is a government service, not a brand)
images.research_notes: Frontal, evenly lit, with good embossed relief and wear. 2612x1988: enough for an object, borderline for B. Sign, not advertising. Hand-painted alternate: NPM "Go Marines! York Post Office" shield sign, filed under painted-wall.

images.what_it_shows: Colour photograph of a sheet of stamped ceiling tin (rock-face/ashlar block pattern) painted as the Texas flag and screwed to a red ranch fence; sunlit, frontal, with dents, buckles and screw heads.
images.people_or_logos: none; state flag motif (white star on blue at left) - keep the crop on the white and red fields
images.research_notes: Colour plus real relief in raking sun; the dents and buckling make it read as thin metal, though the paint is matte (no specular sheen). The pattern is a simple stamped block design, not a Victorian rosette. 1:1 square crop on the white/red fields, clear of the blue and the star: x0,y0,x1,y1 = 0.525,0.19,0.885,0.73 (2650 px). images.title: An abandoned building clad in painted sheets of tin in Emory, the seat of Rains County in East Texas

images.archive_detail: Library of Congress (Carol M. Highsmith Archive)

images.what_it_shows: Frontal colour photograph of a false-front store clad in overlapping sheets of stamped brick-pattern tin, painted sage green over cream with ochre weathering streaks; a corrugated band, a tin awning on tie rods, porch posts and shut doors below.

images.title: Wunderlich showrooms, Brisbane, 1913
images.archive_detail: Wikimedia Commons (John Oxley Library, State Library of Queensland)
images.what_it_shows: A 600-dpi scan of a 1913 newspaper halftone advertisement headed 'A QUEENSLAND INDUSTRY. The Home Beautified by the installation of the Wunderlich System of Interior Decoration...', with two halftone photographs of the Wunderlich showrooms (363-5 Queen Street, Brisbane). The photographs show pressed-metal ceilings, friezes and panelling, display plaques, stained-glass doors and fittings. Caption 'WUNDERLICH SHOWROOMS.', with a handwritten '1913' at top right.
images.people_or_logos: No people anywhere in the clipping. Figures: a seated lion (or dog) sculpture on the floor of the right photo, and round decorative plates and plaques on the walls (no faces). One small pale object beside the chair in the left photo may be a statuette; the coarse screen is too blurred to tell, and it lies outside the suggested crop. Text: headline and caption type, plus the advertiser's name 'Wunderlich' (an old Australian pressed-metal firm), all outside the suggested crop. No modern logos.
images.use: 09: A 1913 newspaper display ad printed in halftone, its photograph of a pressed-metal showroom filling the frame at 1:1, the mark cut out as paper (treatment C).
images.research_notes: A real coarse newspaper screen with paper grain, ink spread and uneven dots, not 'perfect dots'. DOT SPACING: 10.0 px between dot centres along a 45-degree screen (2-D FFT period 9.9-10.05 px at six places; about 60 lpi at the scan's 600 dpi). At 1:1 the dots are clearly separate. It is also an advertisement for pressed-metal interiors, so it ties the halftone beat back to the tin. 1:1 square crop = the right photograph (ceiling, frieze, pilaster, doors, lion): x0,y0,x1,y1 = 0.495,0.193,0.984,0.832 (2938 px). Alternative crop on the ceiling and frieze: x 0.62-0.98, y 0.19-0.66 (about 2160 px). Grayscale TIFF 6000x4603, 27,652,500 bytes, sha1 6e3435c0ea035db7b1935c1174cb04b4cecbacee matches Commons. images.title: The Tropics neon sign was rescued and then restored next to the site where a McDonald's restaurant replaced the demolished Tropics Restaurant in Lincoln, Illinois. According to legend, Vince Schwenoha traveled to California and drew inspiration from its palm trees when he founded the Tropics restaurant in Lincoln and designed its iconic neon sign in 1950
images.archive_detail: Library of Congress (Prints & Photographs, Carol M. Highsmith Archive)
images.what_it_shows: Carol M. Highsmith, 13 Oct 2019, Lincoln, Ill. (Route 66): the restored 1950 neon sign of the Tropics restaurant, lit at dusk. A green-tubed palm tree with a yellow trunk, red neon script 'the Tropics', red 'COFFEE SHOP', green 'DINING ROOM' and 'COCKTAIL LOUNGE' on a dark boomerang panel on two white posts; deep blue sky.
images.people_or_logos: None in the crop. Outside it, far in the background: one person (a worker in white) by a building at lower left (about x 0.02-0.04, y 0.68-0.72); a lit 'King Buffet' sign and Dollar General and Goodwill signs at right (x > 0.55, y 0.54-0.68). Do not widen the crop left or down.
images.use: X29: Strobe extra: the lit sign fills the frame; the mark is a paper void (C).
images.research_notes: Square crop [0.09, 0.125, 0.49, 0.623] (4129 px): the palm end of the sign (palm, 'COFFEE SHOP', 'Tr...', 'DINING', 'COCKTAIL') on dusk blue. The whole sign is about 2.6:1, so no square holds all of it at frame-filling size. Defunct: the LoC caption (photographer's information) says a McDonald's restaurant 'replaced the demolished Tropics Restaurant in Lincoln, Illinois'; the sign, designed in 1950 by founder Vince Schwenoha, was rescued and restored next to the site. Strongest image: real bent tubes read clearly, two colours plus a plant shape. Master is the 8-bit u.tif; a 16-bit a.tif of the same pixels also exists.

images.title: Art deco-style sign for an unnamed hotel (at least on the sign) in Tucson, Arizona. It belongs to a vintage property that now (2018) is a Quality Inn property
images.archive_detail: Library of Congress (Prints & Photographs, Carol M. Highsmith Archive)
images.what_it_shows: Highsmith, 14 Mar 2018, Tucson, Ariz.: a vertical art-deco hotel sign lit at night. White serif letters H-O-T-E-L on teal tiles, each with a double cyan neon sweep shaped like a 'C', on pure black.
images.people_or_logos: None in the crop. Above the sign is an unlit 'Flamingo' script nameboard (its cyan-lit underside ends at y 0.293). Unlit Quality Inn logo panels are above it and below the sign (y < 0.17 and y > 0.86). All of these are invisible at normal exposure (seen only when brightened 4-6x) and outside the crop. Streetlamp at left (x 0.14, y 0.75), also outside.
images.use: X30: Strobe extra: the lit sign fills the frame; the mark is a paper void (C).
images.research_notes: Square crop [0.19, 0.3, 0.863, 0.83] (4650 px): the whole HOTEL column with its sweeps, on black. Generic word only (HOTEL), so the business status does not matter. The LoC caption calls it a sign 'for an unnamed hotel (at least on the sign)' on a vintage property that 'now (2018) is a Quality Inn property'. Keep the crop inside y 0.30-0.83 to keep that brand out. The sign itself is undated (mid-century art-deco style). Very clean, one colour, almost wordless when cropped tighter.

images.title: Vintage, and unusual,  colorful "Sputnik"-inspired sign at the Ace Sign Company's antique-sign museum in Springfield, Illinois. The company has been making signs since 1940 and, over the years, has rescued and displayed many historic neon signs such as this one. Sputnik signs were popular at some U.S. gas stations and other locations in the years after the Soviet Union launched the first artificial earth satellite in 1957
images.archive_detail: Library of Congress (Prints & Photographs, Carol M. Highsmith Archive)
images.what_it_shows: Highsmith, 10 Oct 2019, Ace Sign Co. Antique Sign Museum, Springfield, Ill.: a lit 'Sputnik' sign. A steel ball studded with white, yellow, blue and orange bulbs, with red cone spikes tipped by clear bulbs. The caption says such signs were popular at U.S. gas stations after the 1957 Sputnik launch. The museum's purple-lit wall is behind.
images.people_or_logos: None in the primary crop. Behind the ball, all outside it: a 'Bel-A...' script sign panel at lower right, Heileman's Old Style and Busch beer signs at lower left (living brands), and an unlit dark sign at the left edge.
images.research_notes: Primary square crop [0.375, 0.3, 0.71, 0.674] (2374 px): all ball and bulbs, nothing else. Wider alternative [0.30, 0.093, 0.79, 0.64] (3472 px) shows the star of spikes, but takes in a dark unlit sign edge at the left and a white, letterless strip of the Bel-A panel at the right. No words and no business: a generic star/satellite shape. Bulbs rather than tubes, so it is the 'bulbs' beat. Lit indoors with some ambient light (not pure black). Date c. 1957-1960s.

images.title: Vintage motel neon sign preserved at the Johnson County Arts & Heritage Center in Overland Park, one of the suburban cities surrounding Kansas City, Kansas, which itself is a "sister city" of the larger Kansas City, Missouri, to the east
images.archive_detail: Library of Congress (Prints & Photographs, Carol M. Highsmith Archive)
images.what_it_shows: Highsmith, 3 Apr 2021, Johnson County Arts & Heritage Center, Overland Park, Kan.: the restored 1957 White Haven Motor Lodge sign, lit indoors. White neon script 'White Haven' in a red-outlined free-form cabinet, red 'MOTOR LODGE', a big red arrow outlined in chaser bulbs, and a cyan-outlined 'AIR CONDITIONED / NO VACANCY / TV' panel below; red-lit museum walls behind.
images.people_or_logos: None. Museum exhibit panels behind the lower part (maps, 'VOTE YES!' posters) are outside the crop.
images.use: X32: Strobe extra: the lit sign fills the frame; the mark is a paper void (C).
images.research_notes: Square crop [0.085, 0.025, 0.848, 0.69] (5807 px): script, MOTOR LODGE and the bulb arrow; drops the lower AIR CONDITIONED panel and the exhibit posters. Defunct: the motel closed in June 2010 after 53 years. KCUR, 2 July 2010: 'The White Haven Motor Lodge closed last week after 53 years in operation'; the Johnson County Museum bought the sign at auction for $5,500. Arrow and bulbs plus script.

images.title: Classic advertising neon sign for Kaiser-Fraser brand automobiles, part of the vintage decor of the Choice Auto and Truck Sales dealership in Payson, Arizona
images.archive_detail: Library of Congress (Prints & Photographs, Carol M. Highsmith Archive)
images.what_it_shows: Highsmith, 29 Oct 2018, Choice Auto and Truck Sales dealership, Payson, Ariz.: a round porcelain-and-neon dealer sign, lit indoors. Red neon ring and bands, yellow neon 'KAISER' and 'FRAZER', blue neon 'SERVICE', and painted 'GENUINE FACTORY PARTS &' on a yellow band, hung on a grey wall.
images.people_or_logos: Kaiser-Frazer is a defunct car maker, not a living brand (the name is unrelated to today's Kaiser Permanente). No people. A framed picture at the far left edge and a poster at the bottom right (y > 0.937) are outside the crop.
images.use: X33: Strobe extra: inside the mark (B).
images.research_notes: Square crop [0.065, 0.165, 0.915, 0.921] (5095 px): the whole disc minus the bottom of the ring, which is cut to keep the poster out. Defunct: Kaiser-Frazer Corporation was established in August 1945, renamed Kaiser Motors in 1953, and 'the last Kaisers were produced in America during the 1955 model year' (Wikipedia, Kaiser Motors). So the sign dates from about 1946-1953. Primary colours, block letters, round shape.

images.title: Holiday Motel, Las Vegas, Nevada
images.archive_detail: Library of Congress (Prints & Photographs, Carol M. Highsmith Archive)
images.what_it_shows: Highsmith, 6 Sep 2007, Las Vegas: the Holiday Motel sign at night on pure black. Pink neon vertical 'MOTEL', multicoloured neon script 'Holiday' (pink, yellow and cyan letters with a star over the i), blue neon 'MOTEL', a yellow chaser-bulb arrow, and a pink neon sunburst with five bulb-cluster rays.
images.people_or_logos: No people. Brand caution: the independent motel at 2205 Las Vegas Blvd S opened in 1952 as 'Holiday Inn' (unaffiliated with the chain). Its c. 1957 sign copies the style of that chain's 'Great Sign' (arrow and starburst). It now reads 'Holiday MOTEL', not the chain's mark, but judge whether it reads as Holiday Inn.
images.research_notes: Square crop [0.0, 0.095, 1.0, 0.907] (2805 px): full width, keeps the sunburst, cuts the foot of the vertical L and the arrow's tail. Defunct: 'Motel closed, sign moved off site in 2018' (vintagelasvegas.com); roadarch.com: 'In 2018, sign was removed. It is now in storage at the Neon Museum in Las Vegas.' The largest version is only 2805x3454: there is no TIFF, and this full-size IIIF JPEG matches the stored JP2 to within 1 grey level. It is the lowest resolution here, but the crop is still 2805 px, above 2160. Most colours of any candidate.

images.title: Neon casino sign, Las Vegas, Nevada

images.what_it_shows: Highsmith, between 1980 and 2006 (a scan of her colour transparency), Las Vegas: a casino facade sign at night. 'CASINO' in big gold bulb-studded letters over a fan of red and pink neon stripes, with bulb clusters and chaser lights below.
images.people_or_logos: No people (the entrance area was checked). A small security-camera dome at the bottom centre is outside the crop. Only the generic word CASINO is visible; the casino is not named.
images.research_notes: Square crop [0.125, 0.0, 0.875, 0.95] (4626 px): neon stripes, with 'ASIN' whole and the C and O cut at the edges, and bulbs below. images.title: Neon motel sign ("T Arizonan Motel") from the nostalgic days of automobile travel, saved from demolition elsewhere in Tucson, Arizona and moved to a small grouping of such signs across town outside Pima Community College
images.archive_detail: Library of Congress (Prints & Photographs, Carol M. Highsmith Archive)
images.what_it_shows: Highsmith, 14 Mar 2018, Tucson (Neon Art Walk, Drachman St., by Pima Community College): the Arizonan Motel sign at dusk. A cabinet shaped like the state of Arizona outlined in white neon, yellow neon script 'The Arizonan', red neon 'MOTEL', unlit 'KITCHENETTES / DAILY & WEEKLY RATES', and a yellow 'ENTRANCE' arrow; orange-to-violet dusk sky and tree silhouettes.
images.people_or_logos: None in the crop. Far below it, outside the crop: one small pedestrian (about x 0.67, y 0.95), the Magic Carpet Golf sign with its genie figure (about x 0.6, y 0.78), and a vertical 'Pima Community College' sign.
images.use: X36: Strobe extra: inside the mark (B).
images.research_notes: Square crop [0.03, 0.075, 0.847, 0.665] (4677 px): the Arizona-shaped cabinet and the ENTRANCE arrow, keeping out the other relocated signs below. Defunct evidence: the LoC caption says the sign was 'saved from demolition elsewhere in Tucson' and moved here. roadarch.com: built in 1951 for the Canyon State Motor Lodge, reworked in the 1970s as the Arizonan, removed in 2010, restored in 2012 for the Neon Art Walk. No operating Arizonan Motel can be found. The evidence is weaker than for the others (no closing date), and the face is a 1970s rework of a 1951 sign.

images.what_it_shows: Highsmith, 18 Oct 2016, American Sign Museum, Cincinnati: a liquor-store sign, lit. Red neon 'OASIS' and a neon-ringed clock on a cream arrow-shaped cabinet, green neon 'BEER-WINE / LIQUOR' in a green-edged oval, and orange neon 'TAKE-OUT' on a bar below.

images.title: Good for 5 cents Owney tag

This baggage check was made by John Robbins, who began crafting such tokens in the early 1840s in Boston, Massachusetts.

But for Owney, and his Railway Mail Service companions, the more likely accommodations would be a small hotel or boarding house near the train station. This token represents the latter, with the very apt and descriptive title of “Railroad Eating House & Hotel.”

images.what_it_shows: Frontal painted billboard in the Catskills: a big white script Kutsher's outlined in yellow on a sky-blue field, a 3 MILES AHEAD tab, COUNTRY CLUB and a green GOLF COURSE ON PREMISES band; summer foliage around the board.
images.people_or_logos: A painted golfer figure (with a face) stands at the board's right end (x 0.75-0.93), outside the crop. Kutsher's Hotel and Country Club closed in 2013 (defunct).
images.use: X56: Strobe extra: a painted resort billboard fills the frame; the mark is a paper void (C).
images.research_notes: Square crop (x0,y0,x1,y1) = 0.070,0.210,0.524,0.870 = px 370,763,2766,3159 (side 2396 px); mean luminance in crop 121.4/255; decade 1970s (1977) photo of a 1960s-70s billboard. Saturated blue with flowing script, frontal, sharp. Crop is set left so the golfer is excluded; words are broken by the frame edge. Master u.tif 5281x3631 (57,613,170 bytes, matches the size LoC lists); colour slide scan; the black slide-mount border (about 100-200 px wide) is outside the crop.

made_in_code.title: Tin's paper #F5F1E6 with fine grain and fibres; grain that moves every frame
made_in_code.use: Ground of every shot. Fixed paper (seeded noise and fibres, ~1.7 levels) plus a zero-mean grain field shifted by a frame-seeded offset every frame (~2.3 levels on paper, ~1.8 levels of change frame to frame).

made_in_code.title: The Tin mark with the n's arches refitted as smooth Beziers
made_in_code.use: scripts/markfit.py: least-squares smoothing spline through the traced polygon's arches (max deviation 0.30 and 0.28 viewBox units); every straight edge kept vertex for vertex.

made_in_code.title: 1996 banner GIF: the mark on a 20 px grid in two web-safe colours, ordered dither, hard shadow
made_in_code.use: scripts/web1996.py banner2 --px 20 --fill checker --shadow: web-safe #FF0000 and #FFCC00 in a Bayer 4x4 pattern (a flat orange the 216-colour palette could not show), one-cell black drop shadow. No source image.

made_in_code.title: Search results page, c. 2004 (generic, example.com domains)
made_in_code.use: Set in Liberation Sans (SIL OFL 1.1, Arial's metrics; src/fonts/) at 2.2x a 2004 page, inside the mark, on Tin's deep paper (paper-deep from DESIGN.md). No real engine, brand or site.

made_in_code.title: The terminal: an agent's marketing log on terminal blue #90D7E4
made_in_code.use: SF Mono (refs/brand/fonts) at 46 px, ink at 0.86; the log scrolls one line per beat; the drain floods the mark with ink from the top over one beat.

made_in_code.title: End card: mark, hairline grid, tin.computer, lime cursor
made_in_code.use: Funktional Grotesk Medium; 9% ink grid aligned to the mark's cap line and baseline; lime-cta block cursor, the only lime in the film.
